main_text.p: Et in Iesum Christum filium ejus unigenitum Dominum nostrum.FILIUS est secunda Deitatis persona, à Patre per æternam & incomprehensibilem generationem exsistens, qui Redemtor noster est ad vitam æternam. Matth. 13. versic. 17. Johan. 1. v. 14. 18.34. Cap.3.v.16. Rom.1.v.4.Cap.8.v.32.&c.

Hic in Symbolo dicitur 1. JESUS, quia Servator noster est Doctrinâ, merito & Efficaciâ. 2. CHRISTUS, quia ad nostram salutem est unctus in Doctorem, Sacerdotem & Regem, ut ita nobis adjudicemus Christū, ut Dei Patris donum, ad nos pertinens, eum toto corde apprehendamus; ut nostrū, & certò speremus, eum semper nos salutariter curaturum. 3. Dominus noster, quia nos creavit & recreavit, redemit & ex omni potestate diaboli liberavit.
De Christo Jesu unigenito Filio Dei Patris Domino nostro, Symbolū proponit credenda, PRIMÒ Incarnationem & Nativitatem.
Qui concep-tus est è Spiritu S.INCARNATIO Filii Dei est, quâipse ex SS. Trinitatis decreto, tempore definito (1. Pet. 1. v. 20. Galat. 4. v. 4.) Natu-ram

page.notes: Running head and page number read from the top of the page. Left-margin notes are set in italic. The Latin "Hic in Symbolo" paragraph is roman; the reference line after "FILIUS" is italic. The word "ut nostrū" is printed with a tilde over the u and is copied as printed. The first note is placed beside the opening paragraph; the second beside the paragraph beginning "INCARNATIO". The final word continues on the next page after "Natu-". Long s is written as plain s throughout, and the u/v spelling is normalised only where it appears in lowercase or capitals in the text.
